$schema-note: Canonical Sondalab design tokens. Edit here only; run pnpm gen:tokens.

shared.$font-note: Type (ui-kit 0.30, Lumen): the UI is Geist and Geist Mono; display is Geist too, set 600 with negative tracking. Fraunces is the brand face only (--sl-font-brand: the wordmark and the monogram). The first family of every stack is vendored in packages/ui-kit/assets/fonts and declared in fonts.css (scripts/font-coverage.test.mjs). --sl-text-micro (10.5px) is the micro-label register: mono, uppercase, +0.06em.

font.pixel: "Geist Pixel Square", "Geist Mono", ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, monospace

shared.$radius-note: Lumen radii (ui-kit 0.31): md 8px (controls, fields, callouts), lg 14px (cards, dialogs, overlays), pane 10px (an island pane, between the two). sm stays 6px (rows, tiles, small chrome).
shared.$pixel-note: Geist Pixel Square (ui-kit 0.39, direction D, owner 2026-10-26): the display accent for numerals, the lockup and a single display word. The face draws one pixel cell per 0.08em, so --sl-text-px-1..4 are the only crisp sizes: 12.5px is 1px cells, 25px 2px, 37.5px 3px, 50px 4px. It is proportional (Geist Mono is not), static (one weight) and has no tnum, so a figure that changes in place keeps Geist Mono.
shared.$motion-ease-note: Two curves since ui-kit 0.31 (Lumen): --sl-motion-ease, cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1), for every state change; --sl-motion-enter, cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1), a longer settle for what arrives (a dialog, a tooltip, a toast). Durations stay --sl-motion-fast|mid|slow, which reduced motion zeroes.
shared.$motion-dither-note: --sl-motion-dither-in and -out: how long the hover dither wipe takes to fill a control and to drain from it (effects.js reads them off the host when a wipe starts; ui-kit 0.39, direction D). Not zeroed by reduced motion: the wipe is never armed there, so the control keeps its declared hover.
shared.$motion-spring-note: --sl-motion-spring: a damped spring (stiffness 170, damping 18) sampled into a CSS linear() easing — one ~5% overshoot, then settles. Time-normalised, so it plays at whatever duration token the transition uses. Only for transforms: on a colour the overshoot has no meaning. Re-scope R2 (card spring-tokens), 2026-09-25.
shared.$shadow-note: Casts (ui-kit 0.31, Lumen): black at the alpha each ground needs, never a tinted ink (the pre-0.31 cool ink rgba(28,29,34) is gone). sm is the short cast under a raised tile or key, md a small floating surface, lg the overlay cast (three layers: the overlay's own border in shade is its ring), inset the sunken well of a field. The :root value is the light ramp; each theme re-declares its own in the top-level shadow block.
shared.$focus-note: The focus ring sits flush on the border (offset 0, owner 2026-10-01) and the border takes its colour. Since ui-kit 0.32 (Lumen) a soft halo hugs it: --sl-focus-glow-width more of the ring's own colour at about 22%, off in high contrast and forced colours (components.css).
shared.$viz-note: Categorical data-viz ramp (--sl-viz-0..7): distinct hues for arbitrary series / one-per-item colouring (agent walls, event kinds). Print-ink hues (vermilion, ultramarine, olive, ochre, …). The value here is the no-theme default (the dark ramp) emitted on :root; each theme re-declares the ramp at the lightness that clears 3:1 on its own grounds — see the top-level `viz` block. Not brand accents; independent of --sl-accent-*.

$neutrals-note: The neutral ladder (ui-kit 0.29, Lumen): one [oklch L, C] per role per theme. The generator tints it with each product's accent hue — the token accent for default, agent/accent-registry.json light/dark for every other product, following `inherits` — and bakes LITERAL HEX: themes/{light,dark}.css carry the default product's, themes/products.css every product's under [data-sl-product], neutrals.json all of them for hex-only consumers (Monaco, xterm, Electron, preload, sl-audit). Borders are the generated primary text at the alphas below, and so is the light overlay (`overlay`; dark's stays a black literal in themes.dark); border-lit is white. Chroma stays under 0.04 (colour.js isChromatic): the build fails above it, on gamut clipping, and on two products with different hues baking to identical neutrals. A registry edit is therefore a token change. Paper text-primary sits at the Lumen target's L 0.20 since 0.35 (0.23 until then): the glass glint mirrors its lightness (GLINT_MIRROR - l, 1.17 since 0.35, 1.2 before; scripts/lib/neutrals.mjs) at the same chroma and must stay inside sRGB for every registered hue (the generator checks it), so a darker ink needs the mirror moved with it. code-null is code-comment. High contrast keeps its literals in themes.high-contrast (tile = raised, sunken = canvas, lit = its white edge); any other --sl-* light or dark declares and high contrast does not own is reset to `initial` there, so a high-contrast island inherits nothing.
$label-note: The label on a fill and the step of its hover and press (ui-kit 0.32.1), emitted into tokens.css :root as private MACROS (--_sl-*): channel expressions a relative colour substitutes, so `l`, `c` and `h` are the channels of the colour they are used in, oklch(from <fill> var(--_sl-on)). They live in tokens.css so the theme files, which read them, need nothing else loaded. pole-l: where a label turns from white to the dark pole, on the fill's oklch lightness (0.61 until 0.32.1). pole-dark: the dark pole's oklch lightness (0.22 on the light theme until 0.32.1). hold: the step goes toward black unless the label is the dark pole and would read under this ratio on the fill pressed toward black, then toward white; 4.5 plus the ~0.9:1 a glass pane's tenth of dark page costs a dark label. step: the hover and press lightness steps (the danger tone's). The generator builds --_sl-on, --_sl-lum (the fill's WCAG luminance from its oklch channels), --_sl-lighter and --_sl-step-hover / -press from these numbers; lightening eases chroma by (1 - step / (1 - l))^1.5, the least that keeps every sRGB colour in gamut, darkening dims in linear light.
$accent-note: Accent steps and label (ui-kit 0.32.1). The light theme's label and both themes' hover and active read the kit's own macros (components.css :root), so one rule serves every labelled fill: `step` emits oklch(from var(--sl-accent-default) var(--_sl-step-hover | --_sl-step-press)), the danger tone's step, 0.05 / 0.10 of oklch lightness toward black, unless the label is the dark pole and would read under 5.4:1 (--_sl-hold) on the fill pressed toward black, in which case toward white; the direction is decided once per fill so hover and press move the same way, and the step stays inside sRGB. The label is oklch(from var(--sl-accent-default) var(--_sl-on)): white below oklch L 0.59 (--_sl-pole-l), the dark pole L 0.16 (--_sl-pole-dark) above it. Until 0.32.1 the steps were 89% / 76% toward black on light and 80% toward white / l * 0.92 on dark, and the label's threshold 0.61 with a 0.22 pole. The dark label stays #0A0A0B (oklch L 0.15). High contrast owns its pair and keeps its literal mixes.
$code-note: Syntax-highlight palette (--sl-code-<role>): code is viz, out of the single-brand-accent scope — a chromatic code token stays semantically stable and readable, it does not track the product hue. Since 0.35 (Lumen parity) keyword, string, number, function and builtin are the Lumen target's hues, authored as oklch [L, C, h] and baked to hex by the generator: a triple outside sRGB keeps its lightness and hue and gives up chroma (light function 0.12 -> 0.1077, light builtin 0.11 -> 0.1055), never a per-channel clip. A role may also be a 6-digit hex; `alias` reads one role as another: boolean is number, and tag is keyword since 0.35 (the target has no tag colour, and atom-one's tag sat within OKLab ΔE 1.5 of the new number on paper), so the palette is five hues. Every role clears 4.5:1 (comment/null 3:1) on canvas, surface, raised, tile and sunken of every product, and in an editor on raised under the current line (the primary ink at 4.5%) and under the selection (the product's accent at 18%). The two neutral roles, fg and comment (null is comment), are rungs of the neutral ladder (`neutrals`), so they take the product's tint like every other neutral. Emitted per theme into the theme files and, for hex-only consumers (an editor theme), into neutrals.json beside each product's rungs; high-contrast intentionally omitted (undefined there, consumers fall back).
$viz-theme-note: Per-theme --sl-viz-0..7, emitted into each theme file after shared.viz on :root. High-contrast reuses the dark ramp (its ground is black).
$spectrum-note: Prism (light theme only). --sl-spectrum-0..5 is light (glow: aurora bloom, press, haze), never text, never the only carrier of a meaning. --sl-spectrum-ink-0..4 is the same wheel darkened to >= 3:1 on the light grounds, for anything seen at 1px or as text (rims, aurora --rim/--linear, glitch, halftone, spectral text). Other themes reset both to `initial` so consumers fall back to their accent-derived colour. Not an accent: it never tracks the product hue and never marks state.
$shadow-theme-note: Per-theme --sl-shadow-* (0.31, Lumen): black on every theme, at about 2.6x the light alpha on the dark grounds, where a cast needs it to read. The values follow the Lumen reference's casts with its 1px ring left out: a surface that casts carries its own edge in shade. High-contrast reuses dark (components.css turns depth off there).
